intended_object: An auxiliary function t ↦ exp(∑_{x∈t} x) on multisets of complex numbers, used in the Lindemann-style proof that π is transcendental to expand ∏(1 + e^{α_i}) as a sum over sub-multisets (from the docstring and its uses in the same file).
explanation: The body is `fun t ↦ cexp t.sum`, which is exactly the map in the docstring, so it is correct. But it is not a standard object from the literature. It is a named shorthand that exists only to support the proof: it is mapped over `s.powerset`, `zeroSumPowerset s` and `nonZeroSumPowerset s` so the expanded product can be split into terms with zero exponent sum (each equal to 1) and the rest. So it is a technical device for the proof rather than a mathematical notion to formalize. Mathlib has no separate declaration for it (it is just `Complex.exp ∘ Multiset.sum`). Fixing the domain to ℂ is natural here, since the proof is about complex algebraic numbers.
